summary: Intermittent 503s and long tail latency from gateway buffer oscillation + growing request headers for streaming sessions
description:
Issue summary:
Multiple customers (notably Lumina Health) reported intermittent 503 responses and long-tail (500ms–6s) latency on streaming completions when sessions carry large request metadata. Failures are concentrated on streaming endpoints during sustained KV cache warm-up and at times of high connection churn.

Impact:
- Several production streaming sessions from Lumina Health experienced mid-stream 503s and reconnects, degrading UX for real-time assistants.
- Error rate spike ~2.7% on /v1/streaming/completions for us-east between 2026-03-10T09:10 and 2026-03-10T11:45 UTC.

Environment:
- Hosted API (dedicated capacity) serving in us-east-1; Redwood gateway + AWS NLB in front for TLS termination; internal nginx sidecars and internal api-gateway cluster.

Observed behavior:
- Streaming sessions with repeated small requests and rotating metadata headers (trace IDs, customer-provided context headers) showed progressive header size growth in the downstream path.
- When aggregated header size exceeded proxy buffer thresholds, upstream proxy started buffering then hitting idle/write timeouts, causing mid-stream 503s and connection resets.
- TTFB and token emission delays correlated with periods of proxy flush/backpressure in the gateway logs.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming sessions should maintain steady low p95 latency and not experience mid-stream 5xx due to header/connection buffering.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Start a long streaming completion session against /v1/streaming/completions with a client that rotates per-chunk metadata headers (simulates tracing middleware that appends a small header on each chunk).
2) Send a series of ~40 small messages over 90s; observe request/response headers growth at the gateway.
3) Monitor gateway/nginx proxy logs and stream for 503 or ECONNRESET events when header accumulation crosses ~16KB.

Logs and traces:
- Gateway access logs (excerpt): 2026-03-10T09:22:14Z GET /v1/streaming/completions 503 "upstream-reset" "bytes_sent=12K header_bytes=18.9K"
- Nginx error: "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while sending to client, client: 10.0.4.6"
- Serving runtime trace: increased write stalls during KV warmup windows; per-request queue time spiked to 450ms.
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streaming/streaming-latency?orgId=1&var-region=us-east (spike around 2026-03-10T09:10–11:45)
steps_to_reproduce: Create long-lived streaming session with rotating small extra metadata headers
Observe gateway access logs for header_bytes growth and 5xxs
Repeat against prod us-east cluster to reproduce timing dependency
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: nginx proxy buffer thresholds combined with header growth cause intermediate buffering and then an idle/write-timeout when flush cannot keep up.

Checked gateway and sidecar configs: max_header_size/default_buffer_size set to conservative values (16k). Several customers send extra trace/tenant headers — combined effect pushes size over limit during session.
Observed correlation between KV cache warm-up windows and increased CPU per serving-instance; when backend slower to emit tokens, proxy buffers grow and hit idle timeouts.
Ran capture: tail of gateway connection states showed many FIN_WAIT and slow_writer entries during spikes.
Confirmed not an application-level rate limit: request QPS within expected ranges; increased median backend latency ~120ms during warmup windows is amplifying buffering.
Reviewed related prior tickets: SUP-62177 (mid-stream reset during KV warmup) — similar symptom but that incident was ALB header growth; this one reproduces with NLB+sidecar nginx.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 — Ayesha Khan (Support): Customer reported first occurrence after they enabled a new tracing SDK that appends a lightweight header per chunk. They saw clients reconnect twice in 30 minutes.
2026-03-10 10:22 — Marco Diaz (SRE): Reproduced locally by simulating rotating headers. Confirmed header_bytes passes 16KB threshold after ~35 chunks; nginx starts buffering then returns 503s.
2026-03-10 11:00 — Priya Mehta (Infra): Temporarily increased proxy_buffer_size on staging ingress and disabled proxy_buffering for streaming routes; instant reduction in 5xxs in smoke tests.
2026-03-10 12:05 — Lumina Health (Customer): Confirmed partial mitigation when we instructed them to reduce per-chunk metadata. Asking for permanent fix/rollout timeline.

2026-03-11 09:35 — Marco Diaz (SRE): Runbook link posted: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234ABCD/p1678461234000000 #sre-latency — plan to roll change to production ingress as canary to 10% of traffic.
temporary_workaround: Advised customers to disable per-chunk trace header emission where possible. Support team applied a temporary config on staging ingress: proxy_buffering off for /v1/streaming/completions and increased large_client_header_buffers to 32k for a canary node.
resolution_notes: Partial mitigation deployed to prod on 2026-03-12: updated gateway nginx template to set large_client_header_buffers 4 32k for streaming vhost and disabled proxy_buffering on streaming route handlers. Idle timeout for streaming listeners increased from 30s -> 75s. Results: error rate dropped from 2.7% -> 0.3% in canary, p95 latency improved. Full rollout scheduled 2026-03-14 with follow-up patch to instrument header-size histogram in metrics and add an alert when 99th percentile header size > 16KB.
postmortem_followups: Add automated telemetry: header_size.bytes histogram for streaming routes (priority P0)
Add client guidance to SDK docs about per-chunk headers and streaming best practices
Implement server-side header trimming policy: drop known safe-trace headers if cumulative header size exceeds threshold
Update runbook with steps to toggle proxy_buffering without full deploy
final_status: Partial fix applied to canary; full rollout pending and monitoring in place.
resolution: Workaround + config change applied to gateway; permanent instrumentation and policy follow-ups scheduled.
